sections.heading: Sharing the road: first part — C2
sections.markdown:
FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A68
Keep at least three feet between a motor vehicle and a bicycle. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A68
Do not turn sharply across a bicycle rider's path or force the rider off the road. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A68
Use particular care around bicycles on wet, sandy or gravel-covered roads because these conditions affect them more than motor vehicles. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A68
Check for bicycle riders in the vehicle's path before backing. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A68
Learn bicycle arm signals and, if a rider cannot signal, look for clues such as a head turn or shoulder check before a lane change. [A68]
Source: [A68 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A69
Commercial vehicles are generally larger and less maneuverable than passenger cars. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A69
Commercial vehicles have substantially larger blind spots than passenger vehicles. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A69
Large commercial vehicles need more distance to stop and accelerate and more space to turn. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A69
Give trucks and buses room for a wide right turn, which may start from a left lane to clear a curb or obstruction. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A69
Never squeeze between a turning large vehicle and the curb; wait for its turn to finish before entering that space. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A69
Stop behind intersection stop lines, which leave large vehicles additional turning room. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A69
If uncertain about an approaching truck's or bus's speed, do not turn left across its path. [A69]
Source: [A69 -> src:rdmv-oh-d:ohio-department-of-public-safety-bureau-:handbook:pdf-0069]

Confusables: a motorcycle needs full lane width, while the bicycle rule specifies a passing-space minimum. A flashing motorcycle signal does not establish that its rider will turn. Mnemonic: see, give room, wait. Glossary: a blind spot is an area outside the driver's mirror view; a wide truck turn needs space near the curb. These descriptions restate the source-backed facts only.
